assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin therapy is a complete arc from receptor and hormone biology to drugs that change outcomes in type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit signals now emerging. The discovery is original, clear and of very large clinical and societal impact; it also opens CNS appetite-circuit questions.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 actions and GLP-2, proglucagon biology), Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1, clinical demonstration) and Mojsov (identification of the biologically active truncated GLP-1 form, peptide chemistry) form a plausible trio. Knudsen's medicinal chemistry for liraglutide and semaglutide is a drug-development contribution that could also be argued; with a three-person limit it competes with Mojsov, and the credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many large, independent randomized trials over more than a decade, with consistent effects. Timing is very good given the scale of the therapeutic impact; the biology is stable.
uncertainties: Division of credit between physiology, peptide identification and drug development is contested, notably Mojsov versus Habener-linked work and company-based chemistry, and Habener is not in the credited names.
Four credited names cannot all be accommodated in a prize of at most three.
Long-term safety and durability of weight loss are still being characterized (from my general knowledge, not verified here).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signaling logic: the ER communicates folding stress to the nucleus through IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and downstream branches. It is conceptually original, mechanistically precise and cited across cell biology, with implications for neurodegeneration, diabetes and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Mori (identification of the UPR transcriptional response and the Ire1-Hac1 pathway) and Walter (Ire1 as an unconventional splicing and signaling mechanism, later ISR modulation) are the clear central pair in the supplied credit. The credit appears compact and fair for two laureates.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is robustly and independently confirmed over decades in yeast and mammals. Recognition is timely; therapeutic translation is still incomplete, which is acceptable for a basic-mechanism prize.
uncertainties: Clinical impact is so far mostly conceptual and early-phase therapeutic.
Other contributors (e.g. Ron, Kaufman, Schekman-era secretory pathway work) may be argued by others; I only rely on the supplied credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity with millisecond precision. The method has transformed circuit neuroscience and has begun to reach translational use in vision restoration. The impact and originality are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the hardest part. Hegemann and Nagel/Bamberg established channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Boyden and Deisseroth first used it in neurons; Miesenböck proposed and demonstrated genetically targeted photostimulation earlier. Six names exceed the three-laureate limit. I choose Deisseroth, Hegemann and Miesenböck as a defensible trio spanning concept, molecular tool and neuronal application, while recognizing that this excludes Nagel, Bamberg and Boyden.
assessment.maturity: The technique is replicated in thousands of laboratories and mature. Recognition is timely, but the allocation of credit may be so contested that it delays a prize.
uncertainties: Credit across six names cannot be fairly reduced to three without a visible omission.
Whether the prize should emphasize the discovery of channelrhodopsin or the neuronal application is unresolved.
Clinical translation is limited so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells created a new modality for cancer treatment, with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and approved products. The concept of redirecting T cells with synthetic receptors is original and clinically validated.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical development of CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB costimulation) and Sadelain (CD28 costimulated CARs and preclinical foundations) are central; Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell therapy, TIL and early clinical CAR work. Early receptor-chimera concepts (e.g. Eshhar, Gross) are not among the supplied names, which is an attribution gap I cannot resolve here.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by multiple independent trials and regulatory approvals. Recognition is timely, though toxicity, relapse and limited efficacy in solid tumors remain active issues, and the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: Foundational chimeric-receptor concept credit is not in the supplied names.
Limited efficacy in solid tumors and long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, are unresolved.
Choosing among June, Sadelain and Rosenberg may be disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and the targeting of BCR-ABL turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. The impact is exceptional and the story is clear.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (drug discovery program and compound), Druker (clinical development and demonstration of selective activity) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. Upstream discoveries of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion (Rowley, Nowell, Hungerford, Groffen, Heisterkamp, Witte, Baltimore) are not credited here, which constrains how the prize story is framed.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: more than two decades of survival data and independent confirmation. Timely or arguably late, in view of prior recognition through the Lasker award.
uncertainties: The prize would recognize a drug-development achievement; whether the committee wishes to honor translational chemistry is a judgment call.
Basic-discovery contributors on BCR-ABL are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation transformed the treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor, with large effects on motor fluctuations and dyskinesia, and later opened applications in dystonia and other circuit disorders. It is clinically transformative, and as a practising neurologist I regard the benefit as real and durable for selected patients.
assessment.attribution: Benabid is the only credited name. The prize story historically also involves Delong's subthalamic nucleus basal ganglia model, Bergman's primate STN work, and Pollak and Limousin's clinical work; none are credited here, so a fair prize configuration cannot be supported from the supplied names alone.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of randomized and long-term data; recognition would be timely or even overdue. The mechanism of action remains incompletely understood.
uncertainties: Credit is incomplete with a single credited name; the basal ganglia model contributors are not available to me.
Mechanism of therapeutic effect is not fully explained, and patient selection issues remain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway showed how cytosolic DNA is sensed and converted into cyclic dinucleotide second-messenger signaling, linking innate immunity to infection, autoimmunity, senescence and tumor immunity. It is original and mechanistically elegant, and many of its disease connections are active.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP as second messenger) is the decisive contributor for the sensor; Barber and Ishikawa identified STING (MITA/ERIS from other groups complicates this). Five names are credited and the STING discovery was made nearly simultaneously by several groups, so the trio is defensible but not certain.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism is strongly and independently confirmed. Clinical translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) has not yet produced approved therapies, so recognition might be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical validation in autoimmune disease and cancer is not established.
STING discovery was near-simultaneous across groups, including names not in the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like particle vaccines are a rare case of cancer prevention at population scale, with documented elimination of high-grade cervical lesions and strongly falling cervical cancer incidence in vaccinated cohorts. The impact on public health is very large and the science is clear.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (VLP work with Zhou, Frazer and colleagues; Zhou is deceased and not credited) are the best supported trio. Zur Hausen's HPV discovery has already been honored in 2008, and parallel VLP work by other groups (e.g. Kirnbauer, Roden) complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: more than fifteen years of population data on lesions and, now, invasive cancer. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation among Lowy, Schiller, Frazer and other VLP groups is disputed.
The prize would partly honor vaccine development and public health impact rather than a single discovery.
